title: Our Story - Tsleil-Waututh Nation
edition: Nation website, Our Story page, fetched 9 September 2026

extraction.command:
python3 -c 'import re,html,sys
p=sys.argv[1]
t=open(p,encoding="utf-8",errors="replace").read()
t=re.sub(r"(?is)\x3c(script|style|noscript)[^\x3e]*\x3e.*?\x3c/\1\x3e"," ",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?i)\x3cbr\s*/?\x3e","\n",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?i)\x3c/(p|div|li|h[1-6]|tr|section|article)\x3e","\n",t)
t=re.sub(r"(?s)\x3c[^\x3e]+\x3e"," ",t)
t=html.unescape(t)
t="\n".join(re.sub(r"[ \t\xa0]+"," ",l).strip() for l in t.split("\n"))
t=re.sub(r"\n{3,}","\n\n",t).strip()+"\n"
sys.stdout.write(t)' content/sources/twnation-our-story.html

knownStaleness.topic: A nation speaking for itself, and for nobody else
knownStaleness.problem: This is the strongest kind of source docs/content-review.md 3.2 asks for - the nation's own published account of its own territory, in its own first person - and it covers exactly ONE of the three nations content/levels/vancouver.json names. The quoted sentence is about Tsleil-Waututh territory. The Musqueam and the Squamish are named from a separate page, MST Development Corporation's `The Partners`, which the three nations own jointly and which speaks in all three voices; that page is the level's `nationSource`. A level carries one `fact.source` and one `nationSource`, so the two halves of the statement rest on two different documents and only one of them is registered here.
knownStaleness.action: routed rather than hidden. Either the schema gains more than one source per statement, or a verifier finds one page published jointly by all three nations that states the territory as well as the names. Do not narrow the statement to the Tsleil-Waututh alone: downtown Vancouver is within all three territories and naming one would be a smaller claim than the truth.

knownStaleness.topic: A live nation website with no date on the page
knownStaleness.problem: The page carries news, a strategic plan and video links beside the historical account, so its hash will move for reasons that have nothing to do with the quoted sentence.
knownStaleness.action: when the hash stops matching, re-read the sentence containing `whose territory includes` before assuming the claim moved

knownStaleness.topic: The word `unceded` is deliberately absent from the level's statement
knownStaleness.problem: No treaty covers the city of Vancouver and the word `unceded` is the one nearly every Canadian institution uses for it. This page does not use it, and content/levels/vancouver.json therefore does not either. That is the `say nothing a source does not` rule applied to a word that would have been easy and defensible to write.
knownStaleness.action: if the statement is ever to say `unceded`, cite a page that says it. Do not add the word on the strength of it being true.

grainNote: One web page and one heading. The first flag is about what this document is entitled to cover, the second about how often its bytes move, and the third about a word the statement leaves out on purpose.
